meta.study: obscure-market bids, evidence for the Quick & likely small-market fill (Tj 2026-10-07)
meta.data: Novig published straight trades, 63 day files 2026-08-04..2026-10-05 (the 2026-08-03 file is empty), through the agent proxy; 842 markets still trading within 2 h of the data end dropped
meta.method: tools/research/novig_maker_study.py's static-post simulation, re-used unchanged except: marketType kept per bid, the close window made a parameter, margins 4/5/6/8/10/12, posting times 1/3/6/12/24 h, per-bid staleness kept. A bid on a side at fair/(1+margin), on Novig's grid, FILLS when a later maker fill on that side traded below it (lower bound; 'touch' shown once). Fair stand-in w=0 (Novig's own median of its last 7 trades), w=0.25, w=0.5 (share of the move to the close already known). Close (test A, §62) = median taker price in the 30 min before (last taker trade - the league's longest game), needs >=3 taker trades.
meta.validation: the same code on 2026-09-06..10-04 reproduces RESEARCH.md §88.4 exactly: props+team totals 0.30-0.65 posted 3 h before, 4%: 2,399 bids, fill within 1 h 10%, EV@close +0.85% (w=0) / +3.40% (w=0.25) / +5.13% (w=0.5)
meta.universe: player props + team totals, two-outcome markets, bid price 0.30-0.60 inclusive (QuickLikely.MIN_PRICE/MAX_PRICE), bids that would take (at/above the last traded offer) excluded (0.7%). Tier = MarketPopularity table by LEAGUE|MARKET_TYPE read from MarketPopularity.kt (hot >= $1,000, popular >= $250, obscure < $250 dollars traded per listed market per day); a kind not in the 70-row table = unmeasured.
meta.posting_times: 'pooled' = bids posted 1, 3, 6, 12 and 24 h before the close window (all pooled, intervals resample MARKETS so repeated posts in one market are not counted as independent); 'h3' = posted 3 h before (the §88.4 convention)

horizons.close: filled before the close window opens (= within h hours of posting; this is "before the close", the close itself never contains the fill)
horizons.cut: filled any time up to the end of the close window (the older studies' 'until the close')

metrics.fill_rate: share of POSTED bids that fill
metrics.clv_c: CLV in cents of probability per fill = 100*(close-bid)
metrics.per_bid: EV@close per POSTED bid, % of stake = mean over posted bids of (filled? EV: 0) = fill rate x per-fill edge
metrics.mean_nominal_edge: EV at the stand-in fair when posted, % (the margin plus grid rounding)
metrics.adverse_sel: mean move of the bid side's price from the fair to the close among FILLED bids minus among ALL posted bids (points of %): how much the fill picks the bad moves
metrics.CIs: 95%, bootstrap over markets (2,000 resamples), ratio estimators; day-clustered intervals shown in robustness

close_window_samples.W30: the study definition: >=3 taker trades in the 30 min before the cut (5,058 prop/team-total markets; 4,363 with a bid)
close_window_samples.W60: >=3 in 60 min (8,825 markets), posting times 3 and 6 h, margins 4/6/8
close_window_samples.W120: >=3 in 120 min (13,792 markets), same: a looser, staler close that lets thinner markets in

sample_sizes.obscure_sample_composition: MLB hits+runs+RBIs 79 markets, WNBA threes 74, MLB hits 22, MLB total bases 22, NCAAF team total 17, WNBA double-double 9, NFL receiving+rushing 5, NHL points 5 (thin: 2-4 markets each for longest rush/reception/completion, kicking points, stolen bases)
sample_sizes.unmeasured_composition: 23 markets: EPL/La Liga/Champions League player goals, NFL field goals made, WNBA triple-double and points+rebounds: too few to say anything (111 pooled bids, 18 markets)

coverage.reading: The measurable-close sample is the busiest slice of every tier, and the slice is thinnest for obscure: 1.1% of obscure markets that traded at all (0.2% of those listed) have a close, against 5.3% (2.1%) of popular and 12.1% (9.0%) of hot. Only 18% of listed obscure markets trade at all (hot 74%, popular 40%); the median traded obscure market sees $38 of taker money (popular $174, hot $375). Inside the sample the tier label stops mattering (same fill rate, same edge); across the whole tier it decides almost everything, because it decides whether anyone trades.

findings: (1) FILLS, inside the measurable sample, posted bids filling within 1 h (pooled posting times, 0.30-0.60, w=0.25): 4% margin hot 10.9%, popular 10.1%, obscure 12.2% (CI 9.9%-14.4%, 1067 bids, 241 markets); 6% margin 5.3% / 5.7% / 7.2%; 8% 2.9% / 3.3% / 4.2%. Before the close window (posted h hours before): obscure 25.3% at 4%, popular 27.6%, hot 28.3%. The tier label does NOT change the fill rate once a market is busy enough to have a close.

(1b) FILLS across the whole tier (markets with >=3 prior trades, no close needed; 2,242 obscure markets): obscure bids fill within 1 h 5.7% at 4% against hot 10.8% and popular 8.0% (6%: 3.8% vs 6.2% / 5.2%); and only 0.94% of LISTED obscure markets have that prior activity (popular 7.1%, hot 21.2%). Per bid posted on a random listed market: obscure about 0.035% fills within the hour (6%), popular 0.57%, hot 2.30% (a floor: markets with fewer than 3 prior trades are counted as never filling).

(2) EDGE PER FILL at the close, obscure, within 1 h, pooled posting times: 4% +1.99% at w=0 (CI +0.8 to +3.1), +3.86% at w=0.25 (CI +2.8 to +5.1); 6% +2.54% (CI +0.9 to +4.4) and +5.49% (CI +3.8 to +7.5). Popular at 4%: +1.15% / +3.17%; hot +1.15% / +3.48%. CLV per fill obscure 6%: +1.12c (w=0), +2.42c (w=0.25). Positive with probability >= 99.5% at 6% in all three close definitions and both fairs (robustness.p_edge_positive).

(3) PER POSTED BID (the comparable number, % of stake): obscure 4% +0.239 (w=0) / +0.470 (w=0.25); 6% +0.182 / +0.393; 8% +0.061 / +0.286. Popular 4%: +0.125 / +0.321; hot 4%: +0.136 / +0.379. Inside the sample obscure is not behind. Per bid posted on a listed market the coverage cuts the expected edge to about 0.1-0.14 of popular's and 0.03-0.04 of hot's (coverage.per_posted_bid_yield).

(4) ADVERSE SELECTION (are obscure fills worse per fill?): not detectably, up to 6%. Obscure minus popular per-fill EV, league- and price-standardised, pooled, w=0: 4% -0.05 (CI -1.2 to +1.2), 5% -0.58, 6% -1.18 (CI -3.1 to +0.6), 8% -3.45 (CI -6.1 to -1.0); at w=0.25: 4% +0.03, 6% -0.63, 8% -2.16. Read the intervals as: at 4% a penalty bigger than about 1.2 points (w=0) or 0.9 points (w=0.25) is excluded; at 6% only one bigger than about 3.1 (w=0) or 2.2 (w=0.25) is, so a 1-2 point penalty at 6% cannot be ruled out. The 'filled bids pick bad moves' number (adverse_sel, w=0) is about equal at 4% (obscure -2.7 vs popular -3.4 points) and 6% (-4.1 vs -4.0) but grows faster for obscure beyond: at 8% -6.8 vs -4.2, at 12% -7.8 vs -4.7: the thin-market informed-taker pattern shows up only in deep bids.

(5) WIDER MARGIN does not repair, and there is nothing to repair up to 6%. Obscure per-fill EV (w=0) by margin 4/5/6/8/10/12%: +2.0, +2.3, +2.5, +1.5, +2.7, +3.9; popular +1.1, +1.8, +2.4, +4.1, +5.4, +7.4. Popular's edge per fill keeps rising with the margin; obscure's flattens after 6%: gap -2.6 / -2.6 / -3.5 points at 8 / 10 / 12% at w=0 (significant only at 8% in the 30-min-close sample); the 60- and 120-min-close samples agree in sign at w=0 for 8% (-1.3 and -1.0, league- and price-adjusted; not significant) but not at w=0.25 (W30 -2.2, W60 +0.9, W120 -1.4 at 8%), where the gap only becomes significant at 10-12% (-4.6 and -5.8 league- and price-adjusted, W30). Per posted bid obscure peaks at 4-6% (w=0.25: +0.47, +0.44, +0.39, then +0.29 at 8%) because the fill rate falls faster than the edge per fill rises. 6% is the lowest margin whose per-fill lower 95% bound is clearly above zero in all three close samples at the pessimistic fair (w=0: W30 +0.9, W60 +0.8, W120 +1.2; at 4% W60's is -0.2; at 8% W30's is -0.4).

(6) WHERE IT IS WEAKER: WNBA obscure (threes made and double-doubles, 78 markets) at w=0 earns about nothing (4%: +0.8, CI -0.9 to +2.4; 6%: +0.4, CI -1.9 to +2.6) while MLB obscure (hits+runs+RBIs, hits, total bases and a few others: 128 markets) earns +2.5 (CI +1.2 to +3.7) at 4% and +3.5 at 6%; at w=0.25 both are positive (WNBA +2.9, MLB +3.3). Team totals in obscure leagues (NCAAF, WNBA) are 19 markets: no conclusion. Unmeasured kinds: 18 markets, no conclusion. First half of the window vs second half: obscure w=0.25 6% +4.6 / +7.0, w=0 6% +1.0 / +5.2: positive in both, noisy.

(7) CANNOT SAY: (a) the 99% of traded obscure markets with no measurable close (fewer than 3 taker trades in the 30 min before the close) are not in any per-fill number, and a fill there is the very case 'an informed taker hit a market nobody trades'; the sample gets thinner step by step (W120 admits markets 4x as thin) and per-fill edge does not worsen as the market thins (robustness.activity, all tiers pooled: 3-5 prior trades +3.9% vs 61+ +3.3% per fill at w=0.25, 4%), but that is extrapolation. (b) Queue position and size (simulated bids always fill when a taker trades through; 'touch' upper bound shown). (c) The fair: Vigilant's fair for an obscure line comes from fewer books than for a popular one; w is a stand-in common to all tiers. (d) Nothing here tests the book-count, sharp-agreement or min-sharp-EV safeguards: Novig's trade files carry no book prices. (e) One simulated fill is one taker trading through; real fills are sized and partial.

recommendation.post_obscure_bids_at_all: Yes, as a filler after every popular bid, because in the only slice the data can measure obscure fills are not worse per fill and are positive at 6%; but expect very few of them.

margin.why: per-fill edge buffer is positive with a lower bound above +0.8 in all three close samples at the pessimistic fair; per posted bid it is still >= popular at 4% (w=0.25 +0.39 vs +0.32; w=0 +0.18 vs +0.13: about equal, intervals overlap); 4% touches zero in one sample, 8% loses per-bid value (fills 0.36-0.40x of popular at 4%) and shows the only significant per-fill gap. If the normal margin is raised to 6%, keep obscure at 6-8% (never above 8%).

stake_factor.why: the app sizes stake on the edge at the fair, so a 6% bid already gets about 1.4x a 4% bid's stake (nominal 6.6% vs 4.6%). Measured per-fill edge of obscure@6% over hot+popular@4% is 2.23x at w=0 (95% CI 0.72-4.16) and 1.63x at w=0.25 (CI 1.12-2.28), i.e. per unit of stake the lower 95% bounds are 0.50 (w=0) and 0.78 (w=0.25); 0.5 sizes the stake to the pessimistic bound and also haircuts for the thin markets the data cannot see. Range supported: 0.35-0.7.

recommendation.default: ON (inside the Quick & likely focus, behind every popular bid, off when Quick & likely is off), with the margin and stake factor above. The cost of being wrong is bounded and tiny (half stakes; an obscure bid is about 15x less likely to fill within an hour than a popular one, 0.035% vs 0.57% per bid on a listed market, so the profit it adds is a few percent of what popular bids earn), the data shows no loss at 6%, and Diagnostics counts the obscure fills apart so Tj's own CLV on them is the test.
recommendation.safeguards_note: The trade files carry no book prices, so the data cannot test the min-books, sharp-agreement or min-sharp-EV safeguards; it supports only the margin, the stake factor, the 0.30-0.60 price window and the popular-first order (an obscure bid is ~15x less likely to fill than a popular one). The working defaults in ScanSettings at the time of the run (makerObscureMargin 6%, makerObscureStake 0.5, makerObscureFill on) match what the data supports. WNBA obscure (threes) earns about zero at w=0, so the sharp-agreement safeguard matters most there.
recommendation.review_rule: Judge on the app's own obscure fills: if after about 60 obscure fills their mean CLV is below zero, or EV@close below +1%, turn it OFF; if above +2% at 6%, the margin can come down toward 5%. The simulation cannot see these fills (RESEARCH.md §70.5 uses the same rule: 200+ fills for a firm verdict).
recommendation.if_the_data_said_otherwise: It does not say obscure bids lose at 6%. It does say the measurable evidence is thin (241 obscure markets, 128 fills pooled at 4%, 77 at 6%) and that the benefit is small.
